definitions.explanation: a person who acts with a code of honor to protect the weak and stand up against injustice, often operating outside the law

notes:
A historical term for Robin Hood-like figures in Japanese culture — people who operated outside the law but followed a personal code of honor, protecting the weak and opposing tyranny. Famous examples include {清水|しみず}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{次郎長|じろちょう} and {国定|くにさだ}{忠治|ちゅうじ}. The concept is deeply rooted in Edo-period popular culture and continues to appear in ⟦{時代劇|じだいげき}→時代劇：12968_jidaigeki⟧ (period dramas) and ⟦{任侠|にんきょう}→任侠：24093_ninkyou⟧ films.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {侠客|きょうかく}⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧: chivalrous outlaw film
- {侠客|きょうかく}{気質|かたぎ}: chivalrous temperament
- {侠客|きょうかく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧: the way of the chivalrous outlaw

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{任侠|にんきょう}→任侠：24093_ninkyou⟧: chivalry/gallantry — the code or ethos itself rather than the person; also used as a genre label for yakuza films
- {義賊|ぎぞく}: righteous thief — a thief who steals from the rich to give to the poor
- ⟦やくざ→やくざ：24237_yakuza⟧: yakuza — modern organized crime; while historically connected, lacks the romanticized honor code
